claim_class: Row-only exact redundancy removal plus binary order-chain replacement: same-coordinate integer affine bijection (both directions) with exact objective equality, both affine inverse identities, and target-LP inclusion (reverse without integrality).
claims: 3 claims (cases/test17/preparation.json counts.claims=3): forward integer bijection source->target (290,546 obligations), reverse integer bijection target->source (292,538), reverse without integrality i.e. target LP inside source LP (177,026).

All three carry objective=Equal and the same same-name projection of 57,756 coordinates; only the two integer claims request a complete inverse (inverse=1 / inverse=0). Per-row obligations are VarLower/VarUpper (+VarInt where integrality is kept) for every variable, one check per output row, and literal 'Exact' entries for objective, projection and inverse.
No strictness, point witness or solver claim: cases/test17/README.md:5 - global strictness is not claimed and the report's local order-subsystem point is not promoted to a full-model witness.
proof_encoding: RPA 2, one JSON document: proof.rpa 23,040,341 B -> proof.rpx 15,005,031 B; 3 blocks, each ending in Return{map:[57,756 affine expressions],checks:[...]}; block 0 = 44 Cases steps (binary split, two Witness branches each), blocks 1-2 = 1,798 Lin steps each.

Measured composition of cases/test17/proof.rpa: 3x2,241,375 B Return.map (identical coordinate maps), 2,359,426 B claims (identical 786,365 B projection list three times), checks 4,098,901/4,127,227/2,694,437 B, step bodies 21,221 B and 1,507,417 B x2; request.json 2,359,427 B is three copies of the same projection.
Kernel receipt: obligations 760,110, work 9,432,985, linear_terms 389,448, substitution_terms 1,620,960, branches 44, peak_live_facts 1,798, execute 963,261 us.
reformulation: Same 57,756 binary variables (lower 0, explicit UP 1, one INTORG/INTEND pair), same objective (57,576 nonzeros, exact rational parse), rows 3,757 -> 1,765, constraint nonzeros 499,656 -> 333,408. Deleted: 789 unit packing rows (551 witnessed by an unchanged activation row sum(P)-z<=0 plus z<=1, 238 by a retained larger-support unit row), 257 positive capacity rows (support inside a witness, every coefficient <= RHS), 946 transitive rows of a complete weighted order i*z_i-j*z_j<=0 on 45 binary variables. The 44 adjacent order rows keep their names with coefficients (1,-1): i*sum over the adjacent chain + (j-i)*(-z_j<=0) restores each removed weighted row. Solver objective unchanged (Optimal -237.756627163 -> -237.756681484) and not faster (results.csv test17: 117.64 s -> 118.03 s).
agent_manual_work: Full 620,277-line MPS parse with Fraction coefficients into persistent row/column dictionaries (digest eval 'Parsing exact model representation'), then a second independent fixed-field reader; both reject unsupported syntax.

Structure mining by hand: row-family signatures, exact duplicate row groups (394 groups, 514 excess copies), activation-row index with support intersections (covering_activation), unit packing index (unit_index/covering_unit/maximal_unit), full 45-node pair graph with rank recovery over all 990=C(45,2) rows, union-find connectivity, identical-column scan.

Exact certificates in Python: 1,046 per-row cone identities, 990 transitive restorations, 3,960+176 truth-table evaluations; a local LP witness (z_i=1/i on the pair subsystem) computed and deliberately not promoted.
Text-level MPS writer: drop 1,992 ROWS / 166,248 COLUMNS / 1,046 RHS records, rewrite 88 COLUMNS records, preserve everything else (digest eval 'Writing final certified reformulation').
preparer_helpers: tools/prepare_test17.py (74 lines) defs: prepare, main; imports parse_mps,row_ref (prepare_affine), expression,plus,mul,expr_json,row_fact,sha (prepare_test40), substitute (prepare_test57), Builder (prepare_test88), SparseBuilder,cases_le_shared (prepare_test70), fact,box,exact (prepare_test54).

SparseBuilder.lin (tools/prepare_test70.py:14-31) emits {'Lin':{id,kind,constant,terms}} with an integer-multiplier fast path and asserts the exact residual; cases_le_shared (:32-43) emits a two-branch {'Cases':...} sharing lookup dicts through a ChainMap.
fact/box/exact (tools/prepare_test54.py:16-33): exactness tests on tuple expressions, single-term short-circuit, automatic variable-bound ceilings.
parse_mps/row_ref (tools/prepare_affine.py:20-77): 54-line MPS reader returning vars/var_index/rows/row_index/objective; row_ref maps a row name to {'RowUpper'|'RowLower'|'RowEq': idx}.
friction: No public proof-construction API: all 3,640 rule steps are hand-written dict literals and the arithmetic validating them is an in-generator assert (tools/prepare_test17.py:39); 'Exact' is a literal string in the checks list, so only the kernel re-derives a fact.

Every name and index comes from a from-scratch Python MPS parser (tools/prepare_affine.py:20-73) instead of the canonical model; a disagreement with rpx canonical would be silent because the agent's own verify.py is the only cross-check.

The target is produced by positional MPS text splicing and then re-canonicalized (digest eval 'Writing final certified reformulation': writer_records ROWS 1992 / COLUMNS 166248 / RHS 1046, records_changed 88), although the edit changes no variable, bound or objective coefficient.

Homogeneous obligations are duplicated instead of templated: one 57,756-pair identity projection is serialized in all three claims (786,365 B each, the whole 2,359,427 B request) and each block repeats 173,268 domain checks plus a 2,241,375 B identity map (29.2% of the RPA).

The four negative checks mutate positional JSON paths (tools/prepare_test17.py:63-70, e.g. bad['blocks'][1]['steps'][0]['Lin']['terms'].pop()), so the acceptance harness depends on step ordering and needs a full assemble+verify round trip per mutation to get an obligation index.
